subject: Human Body
title: Melanin and Skin Color
description: A quick win: understand Melanin and Skin Color.

hook.text: Everyone has roughly the same number of melanocytes. Skin color depends on how much melanin each cell produces.

buildup.text: Melanocytes in the epidermis produce melanin and transfer it to surrounding cells.

discovery.text: Darker skin evolved near the equator for UV protection.

climax.text: Skin color is an evolutionary adaptation to sunlight levels.

punchline.text: A tan isn't healthy glow. It's your skin's SOS signal.

quiz.question: Why did lighter skin evolve at higher latitudes?
options: To allow more UV penetration for vitamin D production
To blend in with snowy environments
